item.title: AlphaHits: Full-Event Tracking and Reconstruction Towards a Hit-Level Foundation Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.13222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce AlphaHits, a Transformer-based approach towards hit-level foundation models for LHC physics, building on the TrackFormer and HiggsFormer architectures. AlphaHits operates directly on detector hits and demonstrates scalable full-event charged-particle reconstruction and multi-task event reconstruction and classification from low-level detector information. AlphaHits-TrackFormer reconstructs the full charged-particle content of complete TrackML events without imposing a transverse-momentum selection on the target tracks. It processes both pixel and strip hits in events containing up to $1.5\times10^5$ hits under HL-LHC-like pileup conditions and assigns hits to individual reconstructed trajectories across its kinematic range. This includes the challenging low-$p_T$ population down to approximately $150\,\mathrm{MeV}$ in TrackML samples. It achieves a TrackML score of 0.959 over all reconstructable tracks, representing, to our knowledge, the highest reported TrackML score for full-detector, inclusive charged-particle reconstruction. Building on the TrackFormer architecture, AlphaHits is pretrained on charged-particle tracking and fine-tuned for multi-task reconstruction and classification. From a shared hit-level representation, it predicts tracks, jets, jet flavour, and event-level observables. AlphaHits achieves an AUC of 0.944 for Higgs event classification, with performance comparable to a Particle Transformer (ParT) baseline using fully reconstructed inputs. It also achieves performance comparable to Delphes-based baselines for jet reconstruction, jet flavour classification, and missing transverse momentum regression. These results highlight the potential for scalable full-event tracking and multi-task learning directly from detector hits, representing a promising step towards transferable hit-level representations and general-purpose foundation models for LHC physics.
item.dc:creator: Sascha Caron, Nadezhda Dobreva, Polina Moskvitina, Eugene Shalugin, Javad Sohrabi, Roberto Ruiz, Yue Zhao

item.title: Correlations between $\ensuremath{\mit{\Upsilon}(n\text{S})}\xspace$ production and the underlying event in $\ensuremath{p\!p}\xspace$ collisions with the ATLAS detector
item.description: arXiv:2611.13643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent studies from various experiments at the LHC and RHIC suggest that small collision systems exhibit quark-gluon plasma (QGP) like signatures that were typically observed in large systems. While QGP like signatures have been observed in the soft sector, strong constraints on possible partonic energy loss were established in the hard sector. At the same time, there are multiple pieces of evidence pointing to correlations between hard and soft particle production in proton-proton collisions. The correlations between hard and soft particle production in $pp$ collisions are studied in events with $\Upsilon$ mesons, which provide a valuable hard probe to study such effects. The multiplicity and distributions of kinematic variables of charged particles produced in association with an $\Upsilon$ meson are measured using 139 fb$^{-1}$ of data at $\ensuremath{\sqrt{s}}\xspace = 13$~TeV collected by the ATLAS experiment at the LHC. The measurement is performed separately for the first three $\Upsilon$(nS) states in intervals of their transverse momentum. At low transverse momentum, the associated charged-particle multiplicity is observed to be systematically lower in collisions where $\Upsilon$(2S) or $\Upsilon$(3S) is produced compared to $\Upsilon$(1S), with the difference decreasing as the $\Upsilon$ transverse momentum increases.
item.dc:creator: Baidyanath Sahoo (On behalf of the ATLAS Collaboration)

item.title: Projected sensitivity of the ANUBUIS detector to tau-coupled Heavy Neutral Leptons
item.description: arXiv:2611.14170v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Heavy Neutral Leptons (HNLs) provide a minimal and well-motivated extension of the Standard Model neutrino sector, and are naturally long-lived for small mixing angles between SM neutrinos and HNLs. A previous ANUBIS study determined the projected sensitivity to a single Majorana HNL coupled exclusively to the electron or to the muon, corresponding to the BC6 and BC7 benchmark scenarios of the Physics Beyond Colliders initiative. The present article extends that work to the complementary BC8 scenario, in which the HNL couples exclusively to the tau lepton. As the tau lepton is itself unstable and because charged-current HNL decay modes become available only above the kinematic tau lepton production threshold, the production, decay and event-selection characteristics of this scenario cannot be obtained by rescaling the electron- or muon-coupled results in flavour. The analysis is carried out end to end, from signal-sample generation through acceptance evaluation to sensitivity extraction, with the released SET-ANUBIS~v1.0.0 framework.
item.dc:creator: Camilia Ben Messaouda, Theo Reymermier, Paul Swallow, Oleg Brandt for the ANUBIS Collaboration

item.title: Search for heavy top quark partners with charge 5/3 in the single-lepton final state in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
item.description: arXiv:2611.14335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A search for the pair production of a vector-like quark, X$_{5/3}$, a heavy fermionic partner of the top quark with an electric charge of 5/3, is presented. The search is performed in the final state with one lepton, an electron or a muon. Proton-proton collision data collected by the CMS experiment at the LHC from 2016 to 2018, at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$, are used. Two decay modes are considered. In the conventional decay mode, the X$_{5/3}$ is assumed to decay exclusively into a top quark and a W boson. In an alternative, exotic scenario, it is assumed to decay exclusively into a top quark and a charged Higgs boson, assumed to subsequently decay exclusively into top and bottom quarks. No excess of data events over the standard model (SM) expectation is observed. Expected and observed upper limits on the pair production cross section of the X$_{5/3}$ are set at 95% confidence level as functions of the X$_{5/3}$ mass. The observed exclusion ranges of the X$_{5/3}$ mass extend up to 1630 GeV in the decay to SM particles, and up to 1740 GeV in the exotic decay mode for a charged Higgs boson mass of 800 GeV. These are the most stringent limits on the X$_{5/3}$ decaying to a top quark and a W boson, and the first limits on the X$_{5/3}$ decay into a top quark and a charged Higgs boson.
item.dc:creator: CMS Collaboration

item.title: Active learning at a graduate summer school: feasibility, student response, and the role of instructor training
item.description: arXiv:2611.13583v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Active learning is becoming standard practice in undergraduate STEM instruction in North America and is slowly being adopted in graduate courses. Graduate summer schools, one- to two-week programs in which students from many institutions gather for intensive, specialized instruction in their field, are common in physics; they are taught by researchers chosen for their expertise, and their pedagogy remains almost entirely traditional lecturing. We report a study at a one-week graduate school in neutrino and astroparticle physics attended by 38 students from 8 countries. Six lecturers with limited or no prior experience of teaching with active learning introduced Peer Instruction-style active learning into their lectures after approximately four hours of preparation led by a physics-education specialist. Each of the three main lecture streams was taught traditionally on one day and in the active format on the other. Students were surveyed after each of the first two days and at the end of the week; all six instructors were surveyed as well. In every active lecture, spanning three instructors and three topics, 82-100% of respondents reported that the interactive segments helped them stay engaged and check their understanding, and in every stream the difficulty was rated as better matched on the active day. At the end of the week, 33 of 36 wanted such teaching in future graduate courses, and not one respondent disagreed. All six instructors judged the approach productive and intend to use it again; only two found implementation straightforward. With brief expert-led preparation, lecturers new to active learning implemented it successfully for a heterogeneous audience, and both students and instructors want more. The school was also the first time any of the six instructors implemented structured active learning: a summer school can develop its lecturers as well as its students.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Kamp, Louis Deslauriers, Carlos A. Arg\"uelles, Gonzalo Herrera, William G. Thompson

item.title: Nuclear medium and final state interaction effects in $\eta$ production induced by $\nu_\mu(\bar\nu_\mu)$ at SBN and DUNE energies
item.description: arXiv:2611.13602v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate nuclear-medium modification and final-state interaction in charged- and neutral-current $\nu_\mu(\bar{\nu}_\mu)$-induced $\eta$-meson production on $^{12}\mathrm{C}$ and $^{40}\mathrm{Ar}$. The nuclear medium is described within a local density approximation, incorporating in-medium modifications of the $N^*(1535)$ resonance, which is known to play the dominant role in $\eta$ production through its $N \eta$ decay channel. The subsequent propagation and absorption of the $\eta$ meson in the nucleus are simulated using a Monte Carlo approach. We find that nuclear-medium modifications and final state interaction lead to substantial suppression of the production cross section, highlighting the importance of nuclear effects in interpreting $\eta$ production data. Our results provide valuable theoretical input for the analysis of $\eta$-production at the ongoing SBND and MicroBooNE experiments and the forthcoming DUNE experiment.
item.dc:creator: A. Fatima, S. K. Noor Alam, M. Sajjad Athar, S. K. Singh

item.title: Strong decays of $\psi(3770)$, $\psi(4040)$ and $\psi(4160)$ in four relativistic wave-function representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.13915v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Strong decays provide a direct test of the relativistic structure of heavy quarkonium wave functions. We study the OZI-allowed hadronic decays of the vector charmonia $\psi(3770)$, $\psi(4040)$ and $\psi(4160)$ within the Salpeter equation, using four relativistic wave-function representations $\varphi_1$--$\varphi_4$ that differ in the $S$-, $P$- and $D$-wave components they retain independently, and the revised ${}^3P_0$ model. The quark-pair creation strength is fixed once, by reproducing the measured $\psi(3770)\to D\bar D$ width, and is not readjusted afterwards, so that the results for the two higher states are parameter-free predictions. The representation $\varphi_2$ predicts $94^{+34}_{-23}$~MeV for $\psi(4040)$ and $100^{+23}_{-20}$~MeV for $\psi(4160)$, in agreement with the measured $84.5\pm12.3$ and $69\pm10$~MeV, and it is the only one whose predicted width ratios are compatible with the data. By contrast, $\varphi_1$ overshoots $\psi(4040)$ by $2.5\sigma$, $\varphi_3$ gives the largest widths and is disfavoured at the $5\sigma$ level, and $\varphi_4$, which has no independent $S$-wave component, underestimates $\psi(3770)$ by about $2\sigma$ and cannot be applied to final states containing vector mesons. These results show that a successful representation must contain independent $S$, $P$ and $D$ components, the $P$-wave terms providing the dominant relativistic correction, while the nodal structure of the wave functions accounts for the large uncertainties of the predictions. The mixing angles extracted from $\varphi_2$, $7.92^{\circ}$, $25.8^{\circ}$ and $26.3^{\circ}$, agree with the values obtained in coupled-channel models.
item.dc:creator: Wen-Yuan Ke, Wan-Li Ju, Tianhong Wang, Qiang Li, Guo-Li Wang

item.title: Characterization of BNLs 20 and 30 micrometer thick LGADs for the Electron Ion Collider
item.description: arXiv:2611.14040v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The 20 and 30 micrometer thick Low-Gain Avalanche Detectors (LGADs) produced at Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL) were evaluated. Detailed electrical measurements indicate well-formed and stable gain layers with consistently low leakage currents. Transient Current Technique (TCT) was used to evaluate the gain. Fast-laser timing studies demonstrate time resolutions at the level of a few tens of picoseconds. To assess operational longevity under realistic conditions for Electron-Ion Collider sub-detector systems, devices were irradiated with 30 MeV and 60 MeV protons to fluences of 10^13 to 10^14 neq/cm^2, enabling a focused study of radiation-induced effects on gain stability and timing performance.
item.dc:creator: F. Zareef, J. J. Chwastowski, M. Pycior, I. Ahmad, W. Fryt, G. Giacomini, S. Kusyk, A. Ob{\l}\k{a}kowska-Mucha, P. P{\l}atek, T. Pola\'{n}ski, P. Rze\'{z}nik, J. Swako\'{n}, T. Szumlak, A. Tricoli, D. Wr\'{o}bel

item.title: Nucleon sigma terms in lattice QCD at physical pion mass and in the continuum
item.description: arXiv:2611.14103v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the light, strange and charm $\sigma$-terms of the nucleon in lattice QCD using four $N_f=2+1+1$ twisted-mass gauge ensembles simulated at physical pion masses and with approximately the same spatial volumes. The four lattice spacings ranging from $0.080$ fm to $0.049$ fm, with an action that has O(a) improvement, enable extrapolating the results to the continuum limit. Both valence and sea quark contributions are analysed accounting for excited-state contamination from low-lying multihadron states. We perform global fits to all ensembles, that yield $\sigma_{\pi N}=53.0(7.4)(1.6)$ MeV, $\sigma_s=58.2(17.0)(2.1)$ MeV and $\sigma_c=112(28)(25)$ MeV, with statistical and systematic uncertainties, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Constantia Alexandrou, Christos Iona, Giannis Koutsou, Yan Li, Srijit Paul, Ferenc Pittler

item.title: Angle-Resolved Reflectance Measurements in the Vacuum Ultraviolet for Metallic Samples
item.description: arXiv:2611.14447v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The light yield of noble-element scintillation detectors depends strongly on the reflective properties of detector materials in the vacuum ultraviolet (VUV), where optical measurements are scarce. For this reason, we built a custom rotary setup at IFIC, equipped with a monochromator and operated in a gaseous argon atmosphere, to perform angle-resolved reflectance measurements in the specular reflection plane. We describe the setup and its extensive characterization, together with the procedure used to measure the bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) of materials at various angles of incidence, for wavelengths from 128 to 500 nm, covering both the argon (128 nm) and xenon (175 nm) scintillation wavelengths. To illustrate the capabilities of the setup, we present results for rough aluminum and stainless-steel surfaces as reference materials. Fitting the measured angular profiles with the analytical GGX microfacet model allows us to extract the real and imaginary parts of the refractive index and the surface roughness parameter of each sample. These parameters are then used to extrapolate the in-plane measurements to the full hemisphere and from gaseous argon to liquid media, enabling the inference of the hemispherical reflectance in gaseous argon, liquid argon and liquid xenon.
item.dc:creator: H. Amar, J. \'Alvarez, X. Arrue, C. Benitez, A. Cervera-Villanueva, J. Mart\'in-Albo, L. Molina-Bueno, A. Roche, M. Sorel, J. Soto-Oton, S. Teruel-Pardo, N. Yahlali

item.title: Investigating production of TeV-scale muons in extensive air shower at 2400 m underground
item.description: arXiv:2510.16341v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Deep underground experiments present a new avenue to probe the first interactions in extensive air showers or hadronic interactions in the extreme forward phase space. The China Jinping Underground Laboratory, characterized by a vertical rock overburden of 2,400 m, provides an exceptionally effective shield against cosmic muons with energies below 3 TeV. The surviving high-energy muons, produced in the first interactions of extensive air showers, open a unique observational window into primary cosmic rays from tens of TeV up to the PeV scale and beyond. This distinctive feature also enables detailed studies of charged hadron production in the earliest stages of shower development. Using 1,338.6 live days of data collected with a one-ton prototype detector for the Jinping Neutrino Experiment, we measured the underground muon flux originating from air showers. The results show discrepancies of about 40% corresponding to significances of more than 2$\sigma$, relative to predictions from several leading hadronic interaction models. We interpret these findings from two complementary perspectives: (i) by adopting the expected cosmic-ray spectra, we constrain the modeling of the first hadronic interactions in air showers and provide novel insights into resolving the long-standing muon puzzle; and (ii) by assuming specific hadronic interaction models, we infer the mass composition of cosmic rays, and our data favor a lighter component in the corresponding energy range. Our study demonstrates the potential of deep underground laboratories to provide new experimental insights into air shower physics and cosmic rays.

item.title: Review of experimental studies of charmed meson decays at BESIII
item.description: arXiv:2604.20644v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Experimental measurements of different decays of charmed mesons have been extensively performed at BESIII. Precision measurements of absolute branching fractions of different decays, the decay constants of $D^+$ and $D^+_s$ mesons, hadronic transition form factors of $D$ transitions to light hadrons, $c\to s(d)$ Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa (CKM) matrix elements, tests of lepton flavor universality with various (semi)leptonic $D$ decays, precision measurements of strong phase difference between $D^0$ and $\bar D^0$ decays,amplitude analyses of multibody hadronic $D_{(s)}$ decays, searches for rare $D$ decays have been reported. The reported results offer important information to test different theoretical calculations, to test the unitarity of the CKM matrix, and to search for new physics effects beyond the standard model~(SM). This paper reviews experimental studies of different decays of $D^0$, $D^+$, and $D^+_s$ as well as their excitations at BESIII as of April 15, 2026. Based on existing results of (semi)leptonic $D$ decays from all experiments, we have presented the most precise averages for the CKM matrix elements $|V_{cs}|=0.9686\pm0.0009\pm0.0038$ and $|V_{cd}|=0.2259\pm0.0014\pm0.0013$, the decay constants of $D^+$ and $D^+_s$ $f_{D^+}=(213.1\pm2.0\pm1.5)$ MeV and $f_{D^+_s}=(253.2\pm1.2\pm1.6)$ MeV, as well as the hadronic transition form factors $f^{D\to K}_+(0)=0.7376\pm0.0007\pm0.0013$, $f^{D\to \pi}_+(0)=0.6337\pm0.0053\pm0.0037$, $f^{D\to \eta}_+(0)=0.351\pm0.009\pm0.005$, $f^{D\to \eta^\prime}_+(0)=0.263\pm0.025\pm0.006$, $f^{D_s\to \eta}_+(0)=0.4653\pm0.0058\pm0.0069$, $f^{D_s\to \eta^\prime}_+(0)=0.535\pm0.020\pm0.011$, and $f^{D_s\to K^0}_+(0)=0.627\pm0.036\pm0.009$, where the first and second uncertainties are statistical and systematic, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Yijia Zeng, Xiang Pan, Hailong Ma

item.title: Machine Learning-Based Reconstruction for Resistive Silicon Sensors
item.description: arXiv:2607.11585v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Low-Gain Avalanche Diodes (LGADs) and AC-coupled Low-Gain Avalanche Diodes (AC-LGADs) are promising technologies for precision timing and four-dimensional tracking. In AC-LGADs, the AC pad is coupled to the resistive n$^{+}$ layer through a dielectric layer, while the gain layer remains unsegmented. This structure provides a 100\% fill factor and enables good spatial resolution with a relaxed readout pitch. The same signal-sharing mechanism that makes interpolation possible complicates the readout: charge spreads across multiple pads, the useful information can approach the electronic-noise threshold, and matrix-inversion approaches can become computationally challenging and sensitive to off-diagonal noise. In this work, we study machine-learning-based reconstruction and compression for resistive silicon sensors. We use full-waveform information from correlated pads to regularise the reconstruction and extract spatial information beyond what is available from binary readouts or reduced-amplitude summaries. We first introduce recurrent neural network models based on LSTM layers, which provide a proof-of-concept implementation for full-waveform reconstruction and have been tested for FPGA deployment using \hls. We also study routes towards bandwidth reduction with waveform rasterisation and window-selection methods, and extend the approach beyond the first model to topology-agnostic transformer-based architectures that use pad coordinates as part of the input. These models are designed to support arbitrary pad counts and geometries, mitigate edge distortions, preserve approximately $10~\mu\mathrm{m}$ position resolution for $500~\mu\mathrm{m}\times500~\mu\mathrm{m}$ pitched sensors, and guide future resistive-silicon sensor designs

item.title: Future Muon Physics Experiments: Muon Beams and Experimental Apparatus
item.description: arXiv:2609.25943v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Muons are powerful probes of fundamental physics at the precision and intensity frontiers. We review the status and planned upgrades of selected muon-beam facilities worldwide, together with the experimental apparatus associated with representative experiments across three categories. Charged-lepton flavor violation (CLFV) searches test charged-lepton flavor conservation through rare muon decays, muon-to-electron conversion in nuclei, and muonium--antimuonium conversion. Precision measurements of the muon magnetic and electric dipole moments, muonium spectroscopy, and muonic-atom spectroscopy test the Standard Model and bound-state QED and determine fundamental constants and nuclear charge and magnetization distributions. Muon-scattering programs span low-momentum elastic lepton--proton scattering with PSI MUSE to study the proton radius, lepton universality, and two-photon exchange; high-energy MUonE measurements of hadronic vacuum polarization; NA64$\mu$ missing-momentum searches for invisible dark sectors; and the phased PKMu program, which investigates muonphilic dark matter, light mediators, LFV muon--electron processes, and atomic effects in resonant annihilation. We emphasize the beam intensity, timing, purity, and phase-space control, as well as beamline and detector design, background suppression, and experimental techniques needed to achieve next-generation sensitivity and precision.
item.dc:creator: Yi Yuan, Leyun Gao, Jian Tang, Qiang Li

item.title: Comparative evaluation of future collider options
item.description: arXiv:2511.20417v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In anticipation of the completion of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC) programme by the end of 2041, CERN is preparing to launch a new major facility in the mid-2040s. According to the 2020 update of the European Strategy for Particle Physics (ESPP), the highest-priority next collider is an electron-positron Higgs factory, followed in the longer term by a hadron-hadron collider at the highest achievable energy. The CERN directorate established a Future Colliders Comparative Evaluation working group in June 2023. This group brings together project leaders and domain experts to conduct a consistent evaluation of the Future Circular Collider (FCC) and alternative scenarios based on shared assumptions and standardized criteria. This report presents a comparative evaluation of proposed future collider projects submitted as input for the Update of the European Strategy for Particle Physics. These proposals are compared considering main performance parameters, environmental impact and sustainability, technical maturity, cost of construction and operation, required human resources, and realistic implementation timelines. An overview of the international collider projects within a similar timeframe, notably the CEPC in China and the ILC in Japan is also presented, as well as a short review of the status and prospects of new accelerator techniques.

item.title: Are neutrinos Majorana? Fixed-target and high-energy astrophysical searches decide
item.description:
arXiv:2606.17132v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The original version of this paper proposed a new approach to determining whether neutrinos are Dirac or Majorana fermions, a fundamental open question in particle physics. Conventional searches rely on neutrinoless double beta decay, but this electron-only channel suffers from blind spots. We propose a new, complementary probe to overcome this limitation. A heavy neutral lepton (HNL) triggers a high-energy shift in how the active neutrino flavors ($
u_e$, $
u_\mu$, $
u_	au$) mix---but only if the neutrinos are Majorana. For GeV-scale HNLs, the upcoming beam-dump experiment SHiP can discover the HNL and measure how it mixes with the active flavors. However, the proposed signature of the Majorana nature of neutrinos does not exist. The reasons are explained here. The analysis has been superseded by Ref.~\cite{Barenboim:2026udr}. The original version is retained as v1 for the record.
item.dc:creator: Gabriela Barenboim, Mauricio Bustamante, Qinrui Liu

item.title: High Energy Photon Polarimetry at Lepton Colliders: Quantum Information from Converted Photons
item.description: arXiv:2607.08816v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study high-energy photons produced at a lepton collider that convert into an $e^+e^-$ pair in the detector, as a tool for measuring quantum information observables. We consider single- and double-conversion processes in $e^+e^- \to \gamma\gamma$ and $e^+e^- \to e^+e^-\gamma$. Single conversions enable an in situ extraction of the spin-analyzing power, while double conversions probe polarization correlations. Focusing on the Belle-II detector, we show that, depending on the reconstruction resolution of the opening angle of the conversion $e^+e^-$ pair, quantum correlations of the diphoton system can be probed. In particular, measurements of violations of the Bell inequality, quantum discord, concurrence, nonstabilizerness, and steerability with spatially separated GeV-scale photons can be made at high significance.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Henrique de Lima, Navin McGinnis, David McKeen

item.title: Production Effects and Final-state Interactions in $\pi_1 \to 3\pi$
item.description: arXiv:2607.14300v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the $\pi_1(1600)$ signal channel of $3\pi$ in the $J^{PC} = 1^{-+} \,[\pi\pi]_{1^{--}}\pi~P$-wave. This channel has recently been analyzed by the COMPASS collaboration using the ``freed-isobar" technique which provides direct experimental access to the lineshape modifications of the $P$-wave $\pi\pi$ sub-channel arising from both final state interactions and production processes such as the Deck mechanism. We motivate a unified formalism combining production effects and final state interactions using the Khuri-Treiman formalism, which is consistent with low-energy unitarity, analyticity, and crossing symmetry, seeded by an initial production amplitude. We demonstrate that the precise lineshape of the $\pi\pi$ mass spectrum can be used to determine the relative strength and complex phase of different production mechanisms contributing to the $3\pi$ final state. We conduct a global fit of the $\pi_1$ freed-isobar data set, yielding a multi-dimensional parameterization of the $\pi_1\to3\pi$ decay amplitude at COMPASS as a function of both decay and production variables. We identify the contributions from short-range production and the Deck mechanism and extract the total $3\pi$ invariant mass dependence which will be important for a future extraction of the $\pi_1$ pole position in the $\rho\pi$ channel.
item.dc:creator: D. Winney, S. Gonz\`alez-Sol\'is, M. Mikhasenko, {\L}. Bibrzycki, C. Fern\'andez-Ram\'irez, V. Mathieu, G. Monta\~na, A. Pilloni, L. Qiu, A. Rodas, A. P. Szczepaniak

item.title: Optical characterization and ionizing-radiation response of the BCF-20XL scintillating fiber
item.description: arXiv:2608.21397v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We report optical characterization and ionizing-radiation measurements of the BCF-20XL scintillating fiber from Luxium Solutions, which also wavelength-shifts externally incident blue light (referred to here as Sci-WLS). Attenuation lengths were obtained from transmitted emission spectra using a 3.0 m fiber with a spectrophotometer and described with a two-component attenuation model, yielding a long attenuation length of 6.70 m and a short attenuation length of 0.16 m. The spectral measurements also reveal wavelength-dependent attenuation, with the long component increasing with wavelength and the short component becoming less significant at longer wavelengths. The scintillation response was also characterized under radioactive alpha, beta, and gamma irradiation using SiPM-based readout, providing a benchmark of the detected photoelectron response of BCF-20XL.
item.dc:creator: W. Bae, L. Baker, K. Chen, J. Cho, K. Lang, C. Lee, E. Liang, C. Mathurin, C. Murthy, D. Myers, S. Nguyen, D. Phan, M. Proga, M. Zalikha, J. Zey

item.title: Reconstructing High-Fidelity Light Yield Maps for Surface LArTPCs Using Crossing Cosmic Muons
item.description: arXiv:2608.21581v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Photon detection systems in liquid argon time projection chambers provide prompt scintillation light information that can improve triggering, timing, calorimetry, and interaction reconstruction. These applications require an understanding of the spatial dependence of the detected light yield (LY), which is not adequately described by a single detector-wide average. We present a method for reconstructing voxelized 3D light yield maps in surface LArTPCs using crossing cosmic muons. For each selected muon, the path length through every crossed voxel is converted to deposited energy using a minimum ionizing particle approximation, producing a linear system relating the unknown voxel light yields to the total detected photon signal. The resulting inverse problem is solved using nonnegative least squares, with an additional $L_2$ smoothness penalty used to stabilize weakly constrained voxel values. The method is studied in simulation using the ProtoDUNE-VD detector geometry and photon detection system. Reconstructed maps recover the dominant spatial structure of a visibility-based truth reference and respond as expected to changes in the photon detector configuration. Smoothness regularization reduces zero-valued voxels and localized fluctuations while leaving the detector-average light yield approximately unchanged at the selected regularization strengths. The voxel-wise RMSE relative to the truth reference is reduced by approximately 44% for the regularized reconstruction.
item.dc:creator: Alex Heindel, Wei Shi, Angelo Ralaikoto, Shuaixiang Zhang, Laura Paulucci, Franciole Marinho, Maressa Pimenta Sampaio, Sanskar Jain

item.title: Cosmological Constrained Axion-Portal Inelastic Dark Matter for the LZ Event
item.description: arXiv:2609.17412v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The recent high-recoil candidate event reported by LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) motivates dark-matter scenarios with nonstandard kinematics and momentum-dependent interactions. We study a two-state inelastic dark-matter model in which $\chi_1$ and $\chi_2$ couple off-diagonally to an axion-like particle (ALP) that also couples to gluons and photons. Unlike treatments that assume only one dark-matter state is present today, we track the cosmological evolution of both states. The excited state $\chi_2$ is sufficiently long-lived to survive to the present, with its relic fraction determined by the dark-sector conversion process $\chi_2\chi_2\leftrightarrow\chi_1\chi_1$. We find that this fraction depends strongly on the Lorentz structure of the DM--ALP interaction. Scalar transition couplings lead to nonperturbative conversion rates with a pronounced resonant structure, yielding a final excited-state fraction that varies nonmonotonically with the mediator mass, from $f_2\sim10^{-4}$ to approximately $1/2$ over the parameter range studied. The relative importance of endothermic and exothermic scattering is therefore parameter dependent. By contrast, pseudoscalar transition couplings preserve $f_2\simeq1/2$, yielding recoil spectra dominated by exothermic $\chi_2 N\to\chi_1 N$ down-scattering for the benchmarks considered. Benchmark spectra in all four scenarios can peak near the observed recoil energy of $250\,\mathrm{keV}$. Our results demonstrate that the dominant direction of inelastic scattering in direct detection can be dynamically selected by the early-Universe evolution of the dark sector. With additional data, annual modulation measurements could distinguish these scenarios. We further show that the ALP portal can be directly probed at colliders.
item.dc:creator: Haipeng An, Fei Gao, Jia Liu, Minghao Liu, Changlong Xu

item.title: Constraints on Complex Electroweak WIMPs from Solar Capture
item.description: arXiv:2609.38316v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: One of the most convincing realizations of particle dark matter is provided by models based on electroweak multiplets. The lightest neutral state of such a multiplet can be a stable Majorana fermion or a real scalar, and its phenomenology is governed by two parameters: the dark matter mass and the mass splitting $\{m_\chi,\delta\}$. The sub-MeV range for $\delta$ is particularly important as it allows for a large inelastic scattering cross section. In this paper, we analyze solar capture, energy loss, and annihilation of scalar and fermionic electroweak multiplet dark matter, generalizing earlier results for the Higgsino to other representations. We find that, while the case of a doublet is somewhat special, higher representations behave in a self-similar way. For the higher multiplets, IceCube results constrain the splitting to $\delta \gtrsim 350$ keV for all dark matter masses up to $100$ TeV. Assuming thermal freeze-out and a Standard Halo Model velocity distribution, this rules out most models of electroweak dark matter as a possible origin of the single high-recoil event reported by the LZ collaboration. We also show that a high-velocity tail in the dark matter distribution, such as that induced by the Large Magellanic Cloud, raises the splitting preferred by the LZ event above the solar bounds for many of the multiplets.
item.dc:creator: Juan P. Luengas, Maxim Pospelov, Harikrishnan Ramani

item.title: Exothermic Dark Matter with a Dark Higgs: The LZ 248 keV Event and the Galactic Center Excess
item.description: arXiv:2610.25423v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) reported a $248~\mathrm{keV}$ nuclear-recoil candidate. Exothermic dark matter can explain it in a dark $U(1)$ model whose dark Higgs generates the dark photon mass and the mass splitting. Since the dark photon mass sets both the excited-state fraction and the scattering rate, two dark photon masses explain the event, near $1$ and $25~\mathrm{GeV}$ for kinetic mixing $\epsilon=10^{-4}$. Cosmic microwave background limits exclude most of the lighter branch. On the heavier branch, the southern-sky Galactic Center $\gamma$-ray excess complements the LZ event by selecting a dark matter mass of $40$-$44~\mathrm{GeV}$, and its fit favors a dark Higgs boson near the dark photon mass.
item.dc:creator: Jinheung Kim, Jongkuk Kim, Pyungwon Ko
